key_facts: July 28 UPDATE (Al Jazeera, Reuters/Straits Times, Malay Mail July 28 + Exa search): Malaysia's Rohingya/Myanmar refugee crisis escalated further on July 28 — Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan publicly warned Malaysia should reconsider allowing UNHCR to operate unless it imposes stricter joint screening with the Home Ministry, after Penang's Chief Minister noted 126 Rohingya relocated from Penaga to KL UNHCR (police confirmed valid UNHCR cards, sheltered at KL police HQ). This adds urgent political momentum behind Deputy FM Lukanisman Awang Sauni's July 23 parliamentary disclosure of a 5,000-person Myanmar repatriation plan via naval vessels, though feuding with UNHCR and Malaysia's non-recognition of refugee status still introduce friction vs formal voluntary repatriation. Thailand keeps a narrow edge for its ~80-90k border-camp refugees, formal UNHCR voluntary repatriation framework, and Min Aung Hlaing's Aug 6-7 official Bangkok visit. Shifted Malaysia 0.42->0.45 and Thailand 0.54->0.51 (Indonesia 0.02, Laos 0.01; sum 0.99).
next_review_trigger: FINAL DAY July 29: check Thai/Malaysian official statements on Myanmar refugee voluntary repatriation plans ahead of August 2026.
